newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech share indices rise, funds trade heavily.
newsitem.headline: Czech share indices rise, funds trade heavily.

text.p: Czech shares continued to edge higher on Friday with dealers seeing nothing unusual in the session's trading and investment fund RIF continuing to attract considerable interest.
The PX50 index, which contains no investment funds, rose 0.4 percent to 565.2 and the RPIX, which lists both RIF and SPIF Cesky, gained 0.4 percemt to 1,182.1.

Interest in Czech investment funds took off after rumours began circulationg that many were interested in going open ended, thus allowing for the closing of huge gaps between the net asset value of the funds and their market prices.

SPIF Cesky was among the first investment funds to see large rises in its share prices and the discount from net asset value quickly closed to around 20 percent from nearly 50 percent. Since the gap has closed interest has been transferred to RIF investment fund whose discount is around 40 percent.
"The gap between these two issues is significant - RIF has much larger potential," said Jiri Susicky of Patria Finance.
RIF fell five points to 995, a decline which Susicky attributed to profit taking. SPIF lost two points to 415.
Elsewhere, Komercni Banka posted strong gains, rising 31 crowns to 2,490. SPT Telecom gaind 10 crowns to 3,395, Ceska Sporitelna dropped one crown to 325 and CEZ rose five crowns to 1,072.
"The market was performing quite nicely," said Susicky. "There was nothing really unusual," he added.
Overall, turnover was high at 1.4 billion crowns.
